newsitem.title: BERMUDA: YACHTING-COUTTS COMES BACK TO TAKE BRUT GOLD CUP OF BERMUDA.
newsitem.headline: YACHTING-COUTTS COMES BACK TO TAKE BRUT GOLD CUP OF BERMUDA.

text.p: New Zealand America's Cup hero Russell Coutts and his Team Magic crew came back from the brink of defeat to take the Brut Gold Cup of Bermuda on Hamilton Harbour, Bermuda on Sunday.
The Kiwi team were 2-0 down against Australian Peter Gilmour in the best of five race final before they pulled off three straight wins to take the trophy and the $30,000 first prize.
This puts the Coutts team's earnings from prize money alone this year at over $400,000, and gives them a clean sweep of all five Brut Sailing Series events.
Conditions on Hamilton Harbour proved testing on the final day of the series, as a shifty 20-25 knot easterly breeze sent vicious gusts across the water that had the boats on the edge of control.
Coutts had already survived a tough semi-final, in which England's Chris Law took him to five races.

Things looked hopeless for Coutts in the third race, with a penalty turn to do and time running out, but he managed to spin around at the finish and still take the winning gun to keep his hopes alive.
From then on the New Zealanders took control of the race course, winning the next two races.
Coutts commented at the end of the day, "We weren't going well in the early going today, so we made some pretty aggressive changes.
"We moved crew weight around, and altering trimming techniques, we started using the mainsheet more and putting more twist in the sails."
He added, "I was really pleased, we didn't really expect to win all five Brut events."
Results: 1. Russell Coutts (New Zealand) $30,000; 2. Peter Gilmour (Australia) $18,000; 3. Chris Law (England)
$11,500; 4. Markus Wieser (Germany) $8,500; 5. Ed Baird (U.S.A.) $7,000; 6. Thierry Peponnet (France) $6,500; 7. Jochen Schumann (Germany) $6,000; 8. Peter Holmberg (U.S. Virgin Islands) $5,100.
